memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength. - Deut 6:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the response that the oneness of God demands: love Him with everything. Not a portion of your heart, not your spare time, not what is left over after everything else — but all your heart, all your soul, all your strength. God asks for our total devotion. This is the great command, the summary of what it means to belong to Him. Above all rules and rituals, God wants our love.

Notice that faith, at its core, is not cold duty but warm love. God is not after grudging compliance from us; He desires a relationship of the whole person turned toward Him in affection, trust, and delight. To love God with "all" means there is no compartment of life sealed off from Him — not our work, our money, our relationships, our private thoughts. Every part is meant to be surrendered to Him in love.

Of course, we quickly discover we cannot love God perfectly on our own. Our hearts are divided and weak. But here is the gospel: "We love because he first loved us" (1 John 4:19). Jesus loved God perfectly on our behalf, and He pours God's love into our hearts by His Spirit (Rom 5:5). When we grasp how deeply God has loved us in Christ — giving His own Son for us — our hearts begin to love Him in return. Ask God today to enlarge your love for Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there a part of my life I have sealed off from loving God?
- Do I relate to God more as duty or as love?
- How does God's love for me in Christ stir my love for Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You ask for all my heart, soul, and strength, and I confess my love is often weak and divided. Thank You for loving me first in Christ. Pour Your love into my heart so that I love You more. Amen.
